"Fair" odds are the model's chance turned into odds, with no bookmaker cut. Odds are shown only to compare. They never choose, rank or change a pick. For fun and learning, not betting advice.

02 / Parlays

Best parlays

A parlay joins several picks into one bet, and every pick has to win. So the chance of the whole thing is the picks' chances multiplied together, and it drops fast: three picks that are each 70% likely all win only about 34% of the time. The model chooses these from its own numbers. Odds are never used to pick them.

Build your own

Tap a side in any game to add it, and tap it again to remove it. NBA and NFL games also have spreads, totals and player props: type any line (alt lines too), or let the line finder suggest the line where the model is 70%, 80% or 90% sure. A safer line is more likely to hit but pays less, and the finder never looks at odds.

Combined chances treat different games as unrelated, which is close enough for separate games. Saved odds (moneylines, spreads, totals and prop lines) come from the daily odds check and only cover the sportsbook's main line; alt lines have no saved price, so type it if you have one. Odds you type stay on this device. "Fair odds" are the model's chance turned into odds with no bookmaker cut: when a sportsbook pays more than that, the pick is better value by the model's numbers, though the model hasn't beaten sportsbook closing lines in testing. Bookmaker odds and parlay prices are shown only to compare. They never pick, rank or change anything. For fun and learning, not betting advice.

02 / Power rankings

Who's strongest right now

Rankings come from the same model as every pick, with each team playing every other team once on a neutral court. Odds are never used. For fun and learning, not betting advice.

02 / Game simulator

Play the game out thousands of times

Pick a game. The simulator plays it possession by possession (NBA) or snap by snap (NFL) thousands of times, with real swings: hot and cold nights, minutes, blowouts, turnovers. Its average score is set to the model's own, so it shows the spread of outcomes around the model's pick, not a different pick. Odds are never used.

Simulated before the latest news update, from each team's and player's earlier games. The win chance, spread and total picks elsewhere in the app stay with the main model; the simulator only supplies the shape (ranges, exact-margin chances, player ranges, and which bets tend to hit together). For fun and learning, not betting advice.

02 / Scorecard

How the picks are doing

Every pick is saved before the game starts, so nothing is changed after the result. The betting favourite is the side the bookmakers' odds made more likely, shown only to compare. Odds never pick, change or grade anything. For fun and learning, not betting advice.

Model assessment

Biggest reasons

    Stat comparison

    Each bar shows how much a group of stats pushed the prediction toward one side. Longer bar, bigger push.

    Confident picks vs the betting favourite

    A high hit rate alone doesn't prove an edge: these are often games everyone gets right. So each row compares the model with the betting favourite on exactly the same games. Odds are only used here, to grade, never to pick.

    What matters most

    How much each group of stats moves the model. Bigger share means the model leans on it more.

      Words used here

      Win chanceHow often a side in this spot won in the past. 65% means: out of 100 matchups like this, the favourite won about 65.

      Elo ratingA score that goes up when you win and down when you lose. Beating a strong opponent moves it more. 1500 is average.

      Betting favouriteThe side the bookmakers priced as more likely to win, just before the event. It is a tough benchmark because it already includes injuries, news and expert opinion.

      Test periodThe model learned from older matchups only, then we checked it on recent ones it had never seen. That is where every accuracy number here comes from.
